reader.requirement: At --std 85 a program contained directly or indirectly in another must reach the container's (or any further container's) file connector through a GLOBAL file-name, so that OPEN/CLOSE/READ/WRITE by either program act on ONE connector (open mode, position, status and record area shared, LINAGE-COUNTER global when the FD has LINAGE), for every organization (sequential, relative, indexed) and access mode, while a non-global file-name of a container is not reachable and a contained program's own same-named file is a separate connector.
reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior over InheritStep.cs, InheritedGlobals.cs, DataBindState.cs and LinkageBinder.cs#CallBindExternalAndGlobal; BinderDriver.cs#Bind's per-program connector key (unit.RegistryKey + '::' + name) carries no edition test. The child's bound verbs hold the container's shared FileModel, so the runtime connector is one at every edition. The 85-specific INVALID KEY / AT END requirement (COBOL6826, §1985:VIII/IX SR) is a separate statement rule and counted a USE GLOBAL procedure of the container as applicable.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers sequential files only (direct and indirect container); not exercised there: relative and indexed organizations, a contained program closing/reopening the container's connector, the statement after a FAILED open, global LINAGE-COUNTER, USE GLOBAL, the refusal of a non-global file and local hiding

probes.printed: OUT MF OPEN=35 / IN RLF WRITE=00 / IN XF WRITE=00 / IN LINAGE-COUNTER=3 / IN MF READ=47 / IN XF CLOSE=00 / OUT RLF READ 3=00 R003 / OUT XF AFTER INNER=00 / OUT XF READ K1=00 D2
probes.expected: inner (two levels in) writes relative (dynamic) and indexed (random) files the outer opened; reads the global LINAGE-COUNTER (1 at OPEN + 1 + 1 = 3); READ on the connector whose OPEN failed (35) gives 47; inner CLOSE and re-OPEN OUTPUT of the indexed connector is seen by the outer (its CLOSE succeeds, record D2 read back)

probes.printed: error COBOL1639: 'NREC' is not defined / error COBOL1639: 'NF' is not defined as a file
probes.expected: a non-global file-name and its record are not reachable from a contained program

probes.printed: USE GLOBAL XF 22 / IN AFTER DUP 22
probes.expected: the container's USE GLOBAL AFTER STANDARD ERROR on the shared connector runs for the contained program's duplicate-key WRITE (status 22)
the contained program's own FD SF is a different connector (its WRITE does not create the outer's file): the outer's OPEN INPUT of its never-written file fails 35 and its READ gives 47

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.1.3.7 GR2  (║1.3.7 Sharing Files║)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: A container's GLOBAL FileModel is recorded in the contained unit's InheritedGlobals and found through DataBindState.VisibleFiles; the bound verbs hold the owner's FileModel, whose runtime key is qualified once by the owner, so every program reaches one connector. Every organization probed shares state as required; the path is edition-neutral.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: r2a_status_nonglobal (GLOBAL FDs whose FILE STATUS items LS/HS are NON-global in the container; the inner program OPENs INPUT a missing file and WRITEs an indexed sequential file out of key order): IN SEQ ERR / OUT LS=35 HS=21 / OUT HREC=B1D1 HS=00 / OUT EOF HS=10: the container's status items are updated by the contained program's I/O on the one connector. r2e_relkey_nonglobal (GLOBAL relative random file, RELATIVE KEY a non-global container item set by the container, READ by the inner): IN GOT BBBB / OUT RS=00 RREC=BBBB / IN INVALID / OUT RS=23. r2b_sd_global: SD ... GLOBAL refused COBOL1970 (the 85 SD format has no GLOBAL; X.4.6.3 SR1 names file description entries). r2c_same_record_area_global: GLOBAL FD under SAME RECORD AREA refused COBOL2738 (X.4.6.3 SR3). cite.py: OK §1985:X.1.3.7 GR2; OK §1985:X.4.6.3 SR3. (The 85-only INVALID KEY requirement COBOL6826, §1985:VIII.4.9.3 SR3, fired on an early draft and is a separate rule.)
